lodging.name: Pariwana Hostel Lima
lodging.neighborhood: Miraflores, on Av. Larco facing Parque Kennedy
lodging.highlights: 9.3/10 Superb across 6,100+ reviews — private rooms from ~$25, dead center in Lima's safest and most walkable district, with a rooftop bar, guest kitchen, and genuinely strong security/staff ratings.

lodging.name: Second Home Peru
lodging.neighborhood: Barranco, on the clifftop above Playa Barranco
lodging.highlights: A restored Tudor mansion that was sculptor Víctor Delfín's private home, now an 8-room guesthouse run by his daughter — ocean-view rooms, a private gallery of his work, gardens, and a pool, on a quiet street minutes from Barranco's bars and galleries.

lodging.name: Belmond Miraflores Park
lodging.neighborhood: Miraflores, on the Malecón de la Reserva
lodging.highlights: 89-suite all-suite luxury hotel on the clifftop — rooftop pool with Pacific views, a Peruvian-Asian fusion restaurant, and suites with private saunas or terraces. The splurge that puts you a five-minute walk from Parque del Amor and the paragliding launch point.

itinerary.overview: Lima spent decades getting overlooked as a layover city on the way to Machu Picchu, but it's quietly become one of the best food cities on Earth — the chef Gastón Acurio built his empire here, and the ceviche, Nikkei, and chifa scenes are reason enough for a trip on their own. Add pre-Inca ruins, cliffside parks, sea lion colonies a boat ride offshore, and a permanently mild, foggy microclimate (locals call the gray sky 'garúa'), and three days barely covers the coastline between Miraflores and Barranco.

days.title: Miraflores and Barranco: First Impressions
days.morning: Coffee and people-watching at Parque Kennedy in Miraflores — famous for its resident stray cats — then walk the cliffside Malecón boardwalk south, past the Parque del Amor mosaic sculptures, with paragliders launching overhead if the wind's right.
days.afternoon: Rent a bike (or walk) the malecón cliffside path down into Barranco, Lima's bohemian arts district. Browse ceramics and local crafts at Dédalo Arte y Artesanía, then cross the wooden Puente de los Suspiros (Bridge of Sighs) down to Barranco Beach.
days.evening: Dinner at Clon for Venezuelan-Peruvian fusion — arepas built around fresh local fish — then a nightcap at Juanito de Barranco, a genuinely old-school neighborhood bar that's been open since the 1930s and stays open past 1 a.m.

days.title: Sea Lions, Callao, and Nikkei Night
days.morning: Boat tour out to the Palomino Islands from the Callao terminal — swim with wild sea lions in open water (wetsuits provided) and watch for Humboldt penguins on the rocks. Book direct with a licensed operator rather than a hotel-marked-up tour.
days.afternoon: Lunch at Don Giuseppe cevichería in Callao for their fried-fish sandwiches, then walk Monumental Callao's street-art-covered blocks and small independent galleries — a genuinely off-the-tourist-map neighborhood most visitors skip entirely.
days.evening: Back in Miraflores for a coffee reset at Teoría de los 6 Cafés, then upscale Japanese-Peruvian nigiri at Tomo Cocina Nikkei, and a pisco sour nightcap at Bar Capitán Meléndez.

days.title: Historic Center and a Locals' Ceviche Lunch
days.morning: Breakfast at Caleta Dolsa in Barranco — a surfer-crowd café doing smoothie bowls and strong coffee right near the water. Then head downtown to Plaza Mayor and the Metropolitan Cathedral, built in 1535 on top of a former Inca temple.
days.afternoon: Tour the San Francisco Convent's 17th-century catacombs — underground ossuaries stacked with the bones of an estimated 25,000 people, and one of the odder, more memorable hours you'll spend in Lima. For lunch, skip the plaza-adjacent tourist spots and go to Canta Rana in Barranco, a locals' seafood dive with 17 kinds of ceviche at half the price of the flashier places nearby.
days.evening: One last sunset from the Miraflores malecón or Parque del Amor, then a splurge dinner at Chifa El Dorado — Chinese-Peruvian chifa cuisine on the 18th floor with a citywide view — before a final pisco sour to close out the trip.

tips: Stick to Miraflores, Barranco, and San Isidro for lodging and evenings out — they're the walkable, well-lit, tourist-friendly neighborhoods; the historic center (Plaza Mayor) is worth a daytime visit but isn't where you want to be wandering after dark.
Use Uber or a pre-booked taxi, not street cabs — Lima has a lot of unregulated taxis and airport/taxi scams are a real, well-documented risk, especially arriving late at night.
Eat ceviche at lunch, not dinner — traditionally it's made with the morning's catch, and a lot of cevicherías in Lima close by mid-afternoon because of it.
Canta Rana in Barranco is the locals' ceviche spot — same quality as Barranco's famous tourist-facing places, noticeably cheaper, and a fraction of the wait.

Callao (Monumental Callao specifically) has a rough reputation in parts, but the gallery/street-art district right by the port is safe in daylight and one of the most underrated stops in the city — go with the Palomino Islands boat trip since you're already out there.
Keep phones and wallets in front pockets, skip visible jewelry, and use ATMs inside banks rather than street kiosks — standard-issue Lima advice, but it's repeated everywhere for a reason.
